what_it_does: This paper addresses the challenge of programming specialized hardware accelerators like AMD's AI Engines (custom processors that excel at math-heavy workloads but are hard to program). The authors show how to take familiar programming languages like Fortran and automatically translate them to run on AMD's AI Engines without forcing programmers to learn new languages or rewrite code. They use MLIR, an open compiler intermediate representation, to bridge the gap between high-level language features and low-level hardware operations.
